sentences.text: This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3.

The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 U/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 Bighas 01 Biswas out of the aforesaid acquired LAC no. 78/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Om Prakash & Ors v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 14 land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.
4.

total measuring 28 Bighas and 7 Biswas, having  share by the petitioner no. 1 and petitioner no. 2 to 5 are having equal share of 1/8 each, as per the revenue record situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.
5.
It is stated that the petitioners are the bhumidhar/absolute owner and in cultivatory possession of the said land till the notice under Section 4 of the Act was issued.
The said land is free from all encumbrances and no litigation in respect of the said land is pending before any court of law, and Om Parkash Ors.

6. It is stated that the petitioners have accepted the award amount without prejudice to its rights and has not received the compensation till the filing of the present petition and the petitioners shall accept the award amount under protest.
The Award passed by the learned LAC is highly inadequate and insufficient and not in accordance with the market value prevailing on the date of the notification under section 4 of the Act.

7. As such the present reference petition has been filed on the following grounds :
(i) The learned LAC has not adopted the correct method for calculation the correct valuation of the said land and has made grave error in holding/assessing the market value of the said land based on the old policy of the Government.

The learned LAC has not appreciated the judgment of the superior Courts wherein, it has been observed that "value cannot be so fixed on the information given by the outside Authority or booklet or directory issued by the Government.
The market value of the acquired land is only to be determined by keeping in view the marketability and potentiality of the land".
It is, therefore, prayed that the value of the said land is to be reassessed and to be determined strictly as provided under the law.

(ii) It is stated that the award has been pronounced on 14.09.2005, however, physical possession of the said land has not been taken but the interest has been calculated up to date of award, which should have been taken to the date of payment, therefore, the petitioners have to lose heavy amount of interest on this account.

LAC no. 78/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Om Prakash & Ors v. Union of India Page no.
5 of 14 (iii) The learned LAC has also erred in not including the cost of the crop prevailing on the date of taking physical possession and the whole of the crop of the petitioners were destroyed without giving them opportunity to cut the crop.

sentences.text: No notice for taking the position has been given to the petitioners, therefore, the petitioners have suffered loss on account of distrainment of his crops.

(iv) The learned LAC has also made error in assessing the market value of the said land without considering potentiality of the land as mandated by the Hon'ble superior courts whereby, it has been observed that the prospects and possibilities of future development i.e. potentiality ought to be taken into account in assessing the market value.
Potentiality means such used to which the land to be put in the near reasonable future.
It is the duty of the LAC to take into consideration every intrinsic quality and intrinsic circumstances which tends to push the value either up or down.

The market value was fixed by the Government at the time of notification under Section 4 of the Act without adjustment of amount towards the development charges, however, on the contrary, market value should have been assessed after taking into account the development charges.

The DDA has issued the guidelines/circulars LAC no. 78/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Om Prakash & Ors v.

The DDA and the said land has raised the rate of alternative plots from Rs. 750 per square yards to Rs. 5000/ per square yards, therefore, it is clear that the rates were increased by DDA and the said land has a very high potential value, which is evident from the said effect, that the price of the said land has increasing trend as regarding its market value and after fixation of the rate of agricultural land in Delhi, the prices of the said land has been increased by almost five times.
(vi) The learned LAC has also made grave error by not calling the petitioners for negotiation and the decision has been taken arbitrarily which is against the principles of natural justice.
The ld. LAC has also not considered the status of the said land which is very fertile and levelled and gives 2 3 commercial crops in a year.
The said land hardly needs any development to be done which makes it fit to be used either for industrial or commercial or residential purposes.

(vii) The learned LAC has not taken into consideration that the said land is very close to railway line and metro station, FCI Godown and also surrounded by many developed colonies such as Bhagya Vihar, Roop Vihar etc.

The basic amenities are available in an around the said land i.e. water,
electricity, mettaled road, general market, Post Office, transport facilities, LAC no. 78/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Om Prakash & Ors v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 14 banking facilities,
hospitals, schools, colleges, fire station, telephone exchange, railway station, police Station, farm houses and is very near to NH8, however, the learned LAC has not considered all these factors while passing the said award.

The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.

11. It is submitted that the said land, after acquisition the possession of the land bearing Khasra no.
7//11/12 (416), 12 (700), 14//4 (416), 7/2 (100), 31//3/12 (418), 8 (507), 7/1 (314) has been taken back by the L&B department from DDA and subsequently handed over to RPD VII.
It is submitted that the compensation passed by ld. LAC is legal, adequate, just and fair and the same has been awarded by ld.
LAC after taking into consideration all the factors relevant for determining the compensation, as such the petitioner is not entitled for grant of enhancement of compensation.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition are denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed with cost.

Matter was, thereafter, listed for recording of petitioners evidence.

Counsel for the petitioners as well as Ld. Counsels for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 195 of 2016, Savitri Devi Vs. Union of India.

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
15. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  WHETHER THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT ?
16.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been LAC no. 78/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Om Prakash & Ors v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 14 authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".

During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 05.09.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioners have argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioner in the aforementioned case.
18. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

19. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value as awarded in the case of Savitri Devi (supra) in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

sentences.text:
In the case of Savitri Devi (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 as Rs. 19,45,800/
per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Savitri Devi (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
21. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 22.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2) Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).

(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).

The aforesaid proposition of law has been LAC no. 78/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Om Prakash & Ors v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 14 authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
19. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
